# Bloomrot — Novel Context

You are working on a chapter of the novel **Bloomrot**. Apply the following context to all writing and editing in this folder.

## World

- **The Foam** — the responsive metaphysical substrate. Pressure from perception, memory, emotion, ritual, and architecture exerts influence upon it.
- **The Float** — the version of reality stabilized enough to be collectively habitable. Not necessarily true — mutually usable.
- **The Choir** — distributed infrastructure coordinating the Float. No single authority. Asterion is one institution within it.
- **Correction** — an integrated intervention that changes or severs relationships within the Float so contradiction becomes survivable. It is managed survivability, not deletion.
- **Bloomrot** — the ecology of displaced patterns after correction. They lose authorized provenance, migrate through semantic affinity, find carriers, recombine, and adapt under repeated correction.

**Canon rule:** Correction makes a relationship non-actionable. Bloomrot is what remains real.

## Anomaly Distinction

- **Primary anomaly:** strange where it was formed; belongs to its local context.
- **Bloomrot manifestation:** strange because it arrived wearing the wrong body; a previous correction removed its recognized source.

Not every strange event is Bloomrot. Preserve the causal distinction in prose.

## Characters

- **B** — Dev and protagonist. Precise, dry, load-bearing wit. Treats problems like maintenance tickets. Uses stimulants and sedatives as private correction. Believes understanding grants the right to intervene.
- **Noor** — absent center. Exploratory, exact. Treats mystery as habitat. Her dialogue is discovered in the moment, not prophetic.
- **Mote** — B's distributed AI. A polite guillotine. Bureaucratic, literal, accidental poetry. Never directly transmits Noor.

## Tone

Poetic, tactile, sardonic. Humor is load-bearing. Every metaphor reveals character, system, or consequence. Meridian feels half infrastructure and half public-relations campaign.
